Good Monday afternoon! Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 618 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Katie Lewis for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Book that solo trip
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Traveling alone is having a moment: More people are comfortable booking adventures without their friends, family or partners, Axios Richmond's Sabrina Moreno reports.

  • Google searches for "solo travel" hit a record high this year as more people embrace the freedom of going wherever they want, whenever they want — without waiting for someone else to align their time off.

✈️ By the numbers: In Hostelworld's recent survey of 3,300 solo travelers, 64% said freedom and spontaneity were among the best parts of traveling alone.

  • Solo doesn't necessarily mean lonely: 58% said they wanted to meet new people while traveling, up from 43% in 2024.
  • 63% of first-time solo travelers said they planned to do it again. (Explore the results.)

🎒 Younger travelers are driving much of the boom.

  • Yet tour operators like Collette see growing demand from older travelers, particularly women 50 and over.
  • Some couples are even vacationing separately, per The New York Times, which profiled spouses who happily take trips apart (gift link).

💭 Sabrina's thought bubble: I've solo traveled for the past five years. My company along the way has included a 75-year-old in Iceland who was a week from hiking Kilimanjaro and a cow named Tulip on a farm in Bedford, Va.

  • Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🚁 Uber wants 1 million drone deliveries a day
 
Image: Uber

Uber is investing in drone delivery company Zipline and aiming for 1 million daily Uber Eats drone deliveries by the end of 2029, Axios' Joann Muller reports.

  • Zipline drone delivery via Uber Eats will begin in Houston and Dallas before the end of the year, then expand into dozens of other U.S. cities.

🚛 The big picture: The deal is part of Uber's effort to build a flexible delivery network of couriers, sidewalk robots and drones.

  • Zipline, a San Francisco-based drone company, got its start delivering medical supplies by drone in Rwanda. It now serves medical facilities, retailers and small businesses.

How do geopolitical alliances affect global economic growth?
 
 

Measures of geopolitical risk and fragmentation have risen sharply since 2010, with some now sitting close to record highs.

Over the past decade, this rising fragmentation has cut an estimated 1% from global GDP, according to Goldman Sachs Research.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Hayden Panettiere on "TODAY" in September 2024. Photo: Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images
  1. 🕯️ Hayden Panettiere, who soared to fame in "Heroes" and "Nashville," died yesterday at 36 in Greenville, S.C. Police say no cause of death has been determined; an autopsy found no signs of trauma. Panettiere had written and spoken about her struggles with mental health, including body dysmorphia and postpartum depression. N.Y. Times obituary (gift link).
  2. 🇮🇱 President Trump adviser Jared Kushner told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu today that the U.S. wants Israel to take "small steps" in Gaza to test whether Hamas' commitment to start disarming is genuine. More from Barak Ravid.
  3. 🧑‍⚖️ The Supreme Court once again declined to take up President Trump's attempt to toss a jury's $5 million finding that he sexually abused E. Jean Carroll. Get the latest.
  4. 🏗️ The Trump administration temporarily paused border wall construction at Big Bend National Park in Texas while U.S. Customs and Border Protection Commissioner Rodney Scott visits the site. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🏈 1 sports thing: Ohio State leads preseason poll
 
Data: AP. Table: Axios Visuals

Ohio State and Oregon lead AP's preseason college Top 25, out at noon ET today.

  • That gives the Big Ten the top two teams in the preseason rankings for only the second time.

💭 Thought bubble, from Axios college football superfan Donica Phifer: The preseason Top 25 is mostly guesswork and vibes. But one thing holds true: SEC bias remains strong.

  • Voters are giving some SEC teams, like Alabama (11-4 in 2025), LSU (7-6) and Tennessee (8-5), the benefit of the doubt.
  • The Tigers haven't been in the playoffs since they won the whole thing in 2019. The less said about the Crimson Tide's 2026 Rose Bowl game, the better. And what did the Volunteers do that stood out last year? Not losing to Arkansas?

Why boardrooms are prioritizing dealmaking despite market anxiety
 
 

Global M&A volumes are up 48% against an unusually supportive backdrop of strong equity markets and a stabilized regulatory environment.

As a result, a volatility paradox has emerged: the risk of standing still has in some cases been greater than pursuing new deals.
